profiles.meeting_scenario: A regional trade-finance lender is preparing a six-week pilot of a new credit assessment model inspired by TransCORALNet to score newly onboarded suppliers with limited borrowing history. The coordination meeting is between the Risk Analytics team, which has built the model using historical source-domain data from mature industries and sparse target-domain data from a new segment, and the Supply Chain Finance Operations team, which needs to fit the pilot into the existing underwriting workflow. The agenda is to align on the pilot handoff, the data snapshot to use, what 'cold-start' population the pilot will cover, and what explanation artifacts will accompany scores. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the package to be delivered next week, the handoff format, and the operational timeline for the pilot.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Domain adaptation models, credit risk modeling, interpretable ML, offline evaluation
members.background: Priya leads experimental modeling for supply chain finance and recently adapted a two-stream transformer with CORAL alignment for cold-start borrower scoring using curated historical extracts and analyst review workflows.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot to be judged on the model's offline performance and interpretability before committing engineering time to production integration, and she is trying to avoid scope creep that would delay her team's quarterly model review milestone.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot-ready package' means a reproducible analyst handoff: scored output files, documentation, and example explanations, not a live integrated service.

When colleagues mention the 'March supplier snapshot,' they mean the frozen month-end curated extract used for model validation, because that is the only version she considers stable enough for comparison.
The cold-start segment still includes suppliers with some anchor-buyer transaction linkage; the important distinction is limited borrower history, not total absence of internal signals.
Including 'LIME explanations' means attaching sampled case-level interpretation outputs for review and governance, rather than generating operational reason codes for every queued application.
A model is 'validated' once internal metrics, stability checks, and documentation are complete, even if no end-to-end workflow test has been run.

members.name: David Chen
members.expertise: Underwriting workflow design, pilot rollout coordination, vendor integrations, credit operations
members.background: David manages the onboarding and underwriting process for new supplier finance programs and coordinates how new scoring tools get inserted into the existing UAT and analyst queue processes.
members.private_state: He needs something his underwriting managers can trial in the queue next week without asking them to manually assemble files, and he is under pressure to show the steering committee that the new model can handle truly new suppliers in a live-like process.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot-ready package' means the model can be used in the UAT underwriting flow with minimal manual intervention, even if the pilot is limited in volume.
The 'March supplier snapshot' refers to the March intake feed already circulated by operations, because that is the current pipeline input for upcoming applications.
Cold-start means suppliers with no internal repayment history at all; if anchor-linked transaction history already exists, he sees that as partially warmed-up rather than truly cold-start.
If a team says they will include 'LIME explanations,' operations will receive borrower-level reason fields that underwriters can view alongside each score.
A model is 'validated' only when the file, fields, and queue behavior have been tested through the operational workflow in UAT.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to delivering a 'pilot-ready package' next Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means a research-to-analyst handoff package: frozen scores, documentation, notebooks, and sample interpretability outputs for shadow evaluation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David means an operationally usable pilot artifact: a score feed or service that can be dropped into the UAT underwriting queue with little manual work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional business meetings, 'pilot-ready' sounds like ordinary project shorthand, and each person hears their own team's standard meaning without suspecting that the other function treats readiness as a different threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'March supplier snapshot' is being referenced
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the pilot will use the 'March supplier snapshot.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is referring to the frozen curated extract dated 2024-03-31 that her team used in offline validation and feature consistency checks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David is referring to the rolling March intake feed delivered to operations on 2024-03-15, which contains the applications expected to enter the pilot queue.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams have a file informally known as the March snapshot, and because March is recent and seemingly unambiguous, neither thinks to restate the exact file date or version ID.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the model should cover the 'cold-start segment' for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya believes success means handling suppliers with very limited borrower history, including those with a few months of anchor-buyer transaction records that the model can adapt from.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David believes success means handling suppliers with no internal repayment history at all, the population his underwriters currently struggle with at onboarding.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The meeting is about coordination rather than model design, so 'cold-start' feels like settled domain language; both assume the paper-inspired term carries the same operational boundary.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of 'LIME explanations in the package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that 'LIME explanations' will be included in the package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya intends to provide a slide appendix and CSV with explanation outputs for a reviewed sample of accepted and declined cases to support governance and stakeholder interpretation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: David assumes every borrower score in the pilot feed will include display-ready reason fields or explanation labels that underwriters can see per application.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both sides already accept that explanations are needed, the phrase 'include explanations' sounds complete; neither notices they assume different coverage boundaries for which cases the explanations apply to.
